title: Bubbles
description: Bubbles cinematography fills the air with little lenses: soap films that refract the subject, rainbow edges, wet highlights. Each bubble is an optic, not a disk of bokeh.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A face repeats in a drifting sphere. Joy or threat depends on the light.
Use it when the air should be glass, cheap optics that still photograph. It is the wrong tool for a boardroom, and for sparks that have no film surface.
If the bits are solid motes, you want particles. If the picture is a mirror or a wet street, you want reflections on a plane.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Backlight or side-light soap films so each sphere shows a highlight and a refraction of the face. Keep surfaces: thin-film color at the edge, a wet tick.
The subject remains readable through the swarm. Shallow space helps.
Do not replace bubbles with out-of-focus lamps. Prompt bubbles around the subject: refraction worlds that still read as joy or threat.
Name soap or air bubbles, not bokeh.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for joy, drowning, a spell, an underwater breath. Do not use it as fake bokeh on a night street with no soap films.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Particles are solid, countable motes: dust, sparks, pollen. Bubbles have surfaces and refraction.
Reflections are images on glass, water, or chrome planes. A bubble is a tiny closed optic in the air.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Shape of Water lets water optics and drifting spheres share space with a body. Music videos use soap-film refraction as a lyric field.
Grammar of air as glass, not frames to copy.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Bokeh disks or a particle mist. The tell is circles with no surface, no refraction, no wet edge.
The fix is soap films as little lenses, highlights on a skin of air.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is bubbles in film?
Bubbles are little lenses in the air: soap films that refract the subject, with rainbow edges and wet highlights. Each one is an optic, not a blur disk.
Bubbles vs particles
Particles are solid bits. Bubbles have a film surface and refraction. One you could sweep up. The other is a sphere of air with a wet skin.
When should I use bubbles?
Use them when the air should be glass: joy, drowning, a spell. Skip them in a dry room that only needs dust, and skip fake bokeh.
How do I prompt bubbles for AI image or video?
Write Bubbles around [Subject], refraction worlds. Demand soap-film surfaces, rainbow edges, and the face repeating in the spheres. Do not ask for bokeh lamps.
